newsitem.title: USA: Macy's to downsize Boston downtown store - report.
newsitem.headline: Macy's to downsize Boston downtown store - report.

text.p: Macy's, owned by Federated Department Stores, has decided to downsize its store Boston's Downtown Crossing shopping center, according to a report in the Boston Business Journal.
The 750,000 square foot store, originally home to a Jordan Marsh, also operated by Federated is an anchor in Boston Mayor Thomas Menino's efforts to revitalize the area.

The business weekly reported that Macy's wants to lease out as much as half of the space apparently due to disappointing sales and the need to cut costs. Citing unnamed real estate sources, Boston Business Journal said Macy's is looking to lease its retail basement, as well as the top two or three floors of the seven-story building.
Boston Redevelopment Authority spokeswoman Kelly Quinn said the city was aware that Macy's was re-examining its floor uses and said it's the city's belief the restructuring is limited in scope.
The Macy's downtown downsizing comes just two months after Menino announced that Marshalls would open a new 43,000-square-foot downtown store that would create 100 new jobs.
